question: How many 3-letter words can we make from the letters A, B, C, and D, if we are allowed to repeat letters, and we must use the letter A at least once? (Here, a word is an arbitrary sequence of letters.)
solution:
With repetition allowed, each of the three positions has 4 choices, giving 4³ = 64 words. To count words with no A, restrict each position to B, C, or D, giving 3³ = 27 words. Subtracting leaves 64 − 27 = 37 words with at least one A.
Final answer: 37
